structure.title: A city and a private language
structure.text: Public quarrels establish Verona's violence; private meetings create another way for the lovers to speak.

structure.title: Accelerating decisions
structure.text: Messages, plans, and interruptions repeatedly test whether people are acting with the same information.

people.name: Romeo
people.text: The only son of the Montagues, lovesick over a woman who won't have him, who is talked into going in disguise to a Capulet feast.

people.name: Juliet
people.text: The only daughter of the Capulets, not yet fourteen, whose parents have just begun to talk of a husband for her.

people.name: The Nurse and Friar Lawrence
people.text: Juliet's talkative old nurse and the Franciscan friar Romeo confides in, each of whom tries to help the young lovers in their own way.

context.title: Family honour
context.text: Insults between young men can demand a public response. The households' rivalry makes even apparently private encounters socially dangerous.

context.title: Love poetry
context.text: Romeo begins with familiar poetic formulas. When the lovers speak together, shared rhythm can show a reciprocity that solitary declarations lack.
context.takeaway: Listen for a language made together.

notice.text: Compare the lovers' sense of time with family deadlines.
notice.why: Private hopes must contend with schedules imposed by others.
The timing of knowledge can change the meaning of an action.

opening: Romeo goes to a party expecting to pine for one woman and meets another who changes everything. Juliet discovers that the stranger she wants belongs to the family she has been taught to hate. Their attraction is quick, funny, and mutual; the difficulty is finding somewhere it can exist. Around them, young men defend their honour with swords and parents make plans without asking. Shakespeare makes first love feel expansive enough to contain a whole future, inside a city determined to narrow it.
